Source of truth: `robot_params.yaml` rev **0.2.0-m1-tuned**

These numbers are not guesses. They were swept in simulation against the
stability and reachability gates (`tests/test_gait.py`) before any CAD was
drawn — that is what M1 was for. Typing anything else into Fusion breaks
the guarantee that the simulated robot and the real one are the same robot.

## Fusion parameter names

Create these as **User Parameters** (Modify → Change Parameters) so the
model stays driven by them and a geometry change is one edit, not a remodel:

```
coxa_length   = 45 mm
femur_length  = 90 mm
tibia_length  = 130 mm
mount_half_l  = 70 mm
mount_half_w  = 55 mm
body_height   = 95 mm
splay_angle   = 30 deg
```

## Neutral stance — what the robot looks like at rest

| Joint | Angle | Servo travel | Headroom |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| coxa | 0.00° | [-45°, 45°] | 45.0° |
| femur | 21.08° | [-90°, 90°] | 68.9° |
| tibia | 99.53° | [0°, 150°] | 50.5° |

## Design constraints the CAD must respect

- **Mass ≤ 1500 g total.** This is the binding constraint, not torque. Every gram over eats stability margin and servo life.
- **Reach headroom is only ~24 mm.** The gait already uses most of the leg's span (265 mm max). Do not shorten the tibia.
- **Servo cradle must be swappable.** Standard 40×20 mm footprint fits both STS3215 and MG996R, so the actuator decision stays reversible after printing. Keep the horn coupling as a separate part — the splines differ.
- **Cranium is the electronics bay.** Needs a latched or magnet-held seam; you will be opening it constantly during bring-up.
- **Joint travel** must be mechanically limited to the ranges above so a bad command cannot drive a horn into a printed part.

## Print orientation notes

- Femur and tibia: print **standing on end** so layer lines run along the
  link. Printed flat, they delaminate at the joint under bending load.
- PETG for structural parts (legs, cradles); PLA is fine for the cosmetic
  skull shell, which carries no load.
